Jewish law forbids eating pork.

entries.position: both — a Jewish holiday, Both of his parents are Jewish
entries.contrast: Jewish covers both еврейский (the people) and иудейский (the religion), and many Jewish Americans are Jewish by family and culture without being religious. Use Jewish as the adjective: Jew before a noun (a Jew lawyer) is an insult. Even the noun a Jew can sound blunt, so a Jewish person or He's Jewish is safer. Jewish is not Israeli (a citizen of Israel). The languages are Hebrew and Yiddish, never Jewish.

examples: They send their kids to a Christian school.
Most of the town's residents are Christian.
Christmas and Easter are the main Christian holidays.
Forgiving him was the Christian thing to do.
It would have been more Christian to invite her in.

senses.head: Of Christianity or the people who follow it
examples: They send their kids to a Christian school.
Most of the town's residents are Christian.
Christmas and Easter are the main Christian holidays.

senses.head: Kind, generous and forgiving, as Christianity teaches people to be
examples: Forgiving him was the Christian thing to do.
It would have been more Christian to invite her in.

entries.position: both — a Christian school, Most of the town is Christian
entries.comparison: not gradable — but the 'kind and forgiving' sense grades: very Christian, more Christian
entries.contrast: In everyday American speech Christian is often used to mean Protestant or evangelical: Christian music, a Christian school, even Are you Catholic or Christian? Catholics and Orthodox believers are Christians too. The person is the noun a Christian. Christian name (first name) is British and old-fashioned; Americans say first name. The t sounds like ch: KRIS-chuhn.

entries.meaning: Of Islam, or of the people who follow it. ---
examples: Indonesia has the largest Muslim population in the world.
My coworker is Muslim, so she fasts during Ramadan.
The city has a growing Muslim community.
entries.position: both — a Muslim family, My coworker is Muslim
entries.contrast: Muslim is mainly for people and communities (a Muslim family, Muslim voters); Islamic is mainly for the religion itself, its law, art and history (Islamic law, Islamic architecture). Islamist means political Islam, not simply Muslim. Moslem and Mohammedan are outdated and offensive. Muslim is not Arab: most Muslims live in Asia. Americans say MUHZ-lim; MUUZ-lim and MUUS-lim are also heard.

examples: She went to Catholic school through twelfth grade.
My whole family is Catholic.
The Catholic Church has more than a billion members.
His taste in music is catholic — everything from Bach to hip-hop.
Her reading has become more catholic since she retired.
The creed speaks of 'one holy catholic and apostolic Church.'
Many Protestants recite that creed, and for them catholic does not mean Roman Catholic.

senses.head: Of the Roman Catholic Church or its members
examples: She went to Catholic school through twelfth grade.
My whole family is Catholic.
The Catholic Church has more than a billion members.

senses.head: catholic: including a wide variety of things; broad
examples: His taste in music is catholic — everything from Bach to hip-hop.
Her reading has become more catholic since she retired.

senses.head: catholic: of the whole Christian church, not one branch of it — mostly in old creeds
examples: The creed speaks of 'one holy catholic and apostolic Church.'
Many Protestants recite that creed, and for them catholic does not mean Roman Catholic.

entries.position: both — a Catholic school, My whole family is Catholic
entries.comparison: not gradable — but lowercase catholic, 'broad', grades: very catholic, more catholic
entries.contrast: Capital Catholic is the church. Lowercase catholic (catholic tastes) means broad and wide-ranging, has nothing to do with religion and is mostly written, not spoken. In the US Catholic alone means Roman Catholic. Orthodox Christians are not Catholic, although Greek Catholic (грекокатолический) churches are. Say KATH-lik or KATH-uh-lik.

entries.meaning: Of the Christian churches that separated from the Roman Catholic Church in the 1500s, or of their members. ---
examples: Most of the early settlers in New England were Protestant.
Baptists and Methodists are the two biggest Protestant groups in the South.
He grew up with a strong Protestant work ethic.
entries.position: both — a Protestant church, The early settlers were Protestant
entries.contrast: Stress the first syllable, as in the noun protest: PRAH-tuh-stuhnt. Protestant has nothing to do with today's protesters. Orthodox churches are neither Catholic nor Protestant. Americans often name the church instead (Baptist, Methodist, Lutheran) or just say Christian, which in everyday American speech often means Protestant.

entries.meaning: Of Buddhism or the people who follow it. ---
examples: We visited a Buddhist temple in Kyoto.
He's been Buddhist since college.
Buddhist monks in Thailand wear orange robes.
entries.position: both — a Buddhist temple, He's been Buddhist since college
entries.contrast: The adjective and the person are the same word: a Buddhist temple, a Buddhist, She's Buddhist. The dh is just a d: BOO-dist, also BUU-dist. Russian has буддийский and буддистский; English Buddhist covers both.

entries.meaning: Of Hinduism or the people who follow it. ---
examples: Diwali is one of the biggest Hindu festivals.
Her family is Hindu, so they don't eat beef.
The Hindu temple in our town opened in 2005.
entries.position: both — a Hindu temple, Her family is Hindu
entries.contrast: Hindu is the religion; Hindi is a language of India; Indian is the country. Not all Indians are Hindu, and Hindus also live in Nepal, Bali and around the world. Russian индусский is sometimes used loosely for Indian, but English Hindu never means Indian. The adjective and the person are the same word: a Hindu temple, a Hindu.

examples: Nigeria has the largest population of any African country.
We saw lions and elephants on an African safari.
Her doctor is African, from Ghana.
The museum tells the story of the African diaspora in the Americas.
Kwanzaa is a holiday that celebrates African heritage among Black Americans.

senses.head: Of or from Africa, its countries or its peoples
examples: Nigeria has the largest population of any African country.
We saw lions and elephants on an African safari.
Her doctor is African, from Ghana.

senses.head: Of Black people whose ancestors came from Africa
examples: The museum tells the story of the African diaspora in the Americas.
Kwanzaa is a holiday that celebrates African heritage among Black Americans.

entries.position: both — an African country, Her doctor is African
entries.contrast: Africa is a continent of more than fifty countries, so there is no African language in the singular; name it: Swahili, Amharic, Yoruba. A Nigerian or a Kenyan is more precise than an African. For Black Americans the terms are African American (no hyphen in current style) and Black, while African alone means from Africa.

examples: We spent two weeks visiting European capitals.
Her accent sounds European, but I can't tell where from.
The town square feels very European, with cafés spilling onto the street.
European regulators fined the company $4 billion.
With a European passport you can work anywhere in the EU.

senses.head: Of or from Europe, its countries or its peoples
examples: We spent two weeks visiting European capitals.
Her accent sounds European, but I can't tell where from.
The town square feels very European, with cafés spilling onto the street.

senses.head: Of the European Union
examples: European regulators fined the company $4 billion.
With a European passport you can work anywhere in the EU.

entries.position: both — European capitals, Her accent sounds European
entries.comparison: not gradable — but very European when it means 'typical of Europe'
entries.form: -an from Europe, with the stress moved
entries.contrast: Write a European, not an European: the word starts with a /j/ sound, like a university. The stress moves from YUR-uhp to yur-uh-PEE-uhn. European can mean the continent or the European Union. European countries includes Norway and Switzerland, but European regulators usually means the EU.

examples: Tokyo and Seoul are among the largest Asian cities.
Asian markets fell sharply overnight.
The Asian elephant is smaller than the African one.
The city has a large Asian American population.
She was one of only two Asian kids in her high school in Ohio.

senses.head: Of or from Asia, its countries or its peoples
examples: Tokyo and Seoul are among the largest Asian cities.
Asian markets fell sharply overnight.
The Asian elephant is smaller than the African one.

senses.head: Of Americans whose families came from East, Southeast or South Asia
examples: The city has a large Asian American population.
She was one of only two Asian kids in her high school in Ohio.

entries.position: both — Asian markets, Her family is Asian
entries.contrast: In the US Asian usually means East or Southeast Asian (Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Filipino), while in Britain it usually means South Asian (Indian, Pakistani). Asian American has no hyphen in current style. Oriental for people is outdated and offensive, and survives only for rugs and a few names. The sound in the middle is zh: AY-zhuhn.

examples: Scientists give every plant a Latin name.
Turkish switched to the Latin alphabet in 1928.
Many English legal terms are Latin phrases.
We took Latin dance classes — salsa and bachata.
The station plays Latin pop all day.
Miami has a huge Latin community.
The movie leans on the old stereotype of the passionate Latin lover.
Italy, Spain and Portugal share a Latin heritage that goes back to Rome.

senses.head: Of Latin, the language of ancient Rome, or of its alphabet
examples: Scientists give every plant a Latin name.
Turkish switched to the Latin alphabet in 1928.
Many English legal terms are Latin phrases.

senses.head: Of Latin America, or of its people and culture
examples: We took Latin dance classes — salsa and bachata.
The station plays Latin pop all day.
Miami has a huge Latin community.

senses.head: Of the peoples of southern Europe whose languages come from Latin, such as the Italians and Spanish
examples: The movie leans on the old stereotype of the passionate Latin lover.
Italy, Spain and Portugal share a Latin heritage that goes back to Rome.

entries.position: both — mostly before a noun: Latin music; after a verb mostly of words: The phrase is Latin
entries.contrast: For a person, Americans say Latino or Latina (also Latine or Latinx) or Hispanic: She's Latina, rarely She's Latin. Latin is most natural for music, dance and food, and in Latin America and Latin American. Hispanic points to the Spanish language, so Brazilians are Latino but not really Hispanic. Russian латиница is the Latin alphabet, or Latin letters.

examples: Most Western countries imposed sanctions.
Acupuncture is now used alongside Western medicine.
The city has become more Western over the last twenty years.
They own a ranch in western Montana.
The western side of the house gets the afternoon sun.
He always wears Western boots and a big belt buckle.
The store sells Western wear and saddles.

senses.head: Of Europe and North America, or of their culture, politics and values
examples: Most Western countries imposed sanctions.
Acupuncture is now used alongside Western medicine.
The city has become more Western over the last twenty years.

senses.head: In, from or facing the west of a place
examples: They own a ranch in western Montana.
The western side of the house gets the afternoon sun.

senses.head: Of the American West, or in the style of its cowboys
examples: He always wears Western boots and a big belt buckle.
The store sells Western wear and saddles.

entries.position: both — before a noun in the direction sense: western Oregon; after a verb only in the 'of the West' senses: Their values are very Western
entries.comparison: not gradable — but the 'of the West' sense grades: more Western; the farthest west is westernmost
entries.contrast: Capital Western is for the West as a culture (Western democracies, Western medicine), for the American West (Western boots) and in names (Western Europe, the Western Hemisphere). Plain direction is lowercase: western Kansas, the western shore of the lake. Oregon is western is not English; say Oregon is in the West. A western (a noun) is a cowboy movie or book. For the wind, a west wind or a westerly wind is more usual.

examples: Her family farms in eastern Washington.
The storm will reach the eastern part of the state by evening.
Many Eastern European immigrants settled in Chicago.
The Eastern bloc fell apart after 1989.
The game starts at 8 p.m. Eastern time.
A snowstorm shut down airports up and down the Eastern Seaboard.
She's interested in Eastern philosophy and meditation.
Her paintings have become more Eastern in style since she moved to Kyoto.
Many Eastern Orthodox churches celebrate Christmas on January 7.
The Eastern and Western churches split in 1054.

senses.head: In, from or facing the east of a place
examples: Her family farms in eastern Washington.
The storm will reach the eastern part of the state by evening.

senses.head: Of Eastern Europe, especially the countries once under Soviet control
examples: Many Eastern European immigrants settled in Chicago.
The Eastern bloc fell apart after 1989.

senses.head: Of the eastern United States, especially its time zone
examples: The game starts at 8 p.m. Eastern time.
A snowstorm shut down airports up and down the Eastern Seaboard.

senses.head: Of Asia, or of its cultures, religions and ways of thinking
examples: She's interested in Eastern philosophy and meditation.
Her paintings have become more Eastern in style since she moved to Kyoto.

senses.head: Of the Orthodox churches of Eastern Europe and the Middle East
examples: Many Eastern Orthodox churches celebrate Christmas on January 7.
The Eastern and Western churches split in 1054.

entries.position: both — before a noun in the direction sense: eastern Ohio; after a verb only in the 'of the East' sense: The design looks very Eastern
entries.comparison: not gradable — but the 'of the East' sense grades: more Eastern; the farthest east is easternmost
entries.contrast: Capital Eastern is for Asian cultures (Eastern philosophy), for the former Communist countries (Eastern Europe, Eastern European), for the Orthodox churches and for the US time zone (Eastern time, the time in New York). Plain direction is lowercase: eastern Ohio, the eastern shore. The Middle East has its own adjective: Middle Eastern food. Oriental is outdated for people.

examples: We saw the northern lights in Alaska.
Winters in northern Minnesota are brutal.
The northern half of the state is mostly forest.
Northern troops captured Atlanta in 1864.
After ten years in Georgia, she still has a Northern accent.

senses.head: In, from or facing the north of a place
examples: We saw the northern lights in Alaska.
Winters in northern Minnesota are brutal.
The northern half of the state is mostly forest.

senses.head: Of the northern states of the US, or typical of them
examples: Northern troops captured Atlanta in 1864.
After ten years in Georgia, she still has a Northern accent.

entries.position: both — mostly before a noun: northern Minnesota; after a verb of the US North: His accent is Northern
entries.comparison: not gradable — the farthest north is northernmost
entries.contrast: Lowercase for plain direction (northern California, the northern lights), capital for names and for the US North as a region: Northern Ireland, the Northern Hemisphere, a Northern accent. In US history Northern means the states that fought for the Union in the Civil War. The th is voiced, as in other: NOR-thurn.

examples: We spent a week in southern Spain.
The southern half of the country is much drier.
Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.
Grits and fried chicken are Southern classics.
She has a soft Southern accent.
After twenty years in Atlanta, he's more Southern than the locals.

senses.head: In, from or facing the south of a place
examples: We spent a week in southern Spain.
The southern half of the country is much drier.
Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.

senses.head: Of the American South, or typical of its people and way of life
examples: Grits and fried chicken are Southern classics.
She has a soft Southern accent.
After twenty years in Atlanta, he's more Southern than the locals.

entries.position: both — before a noun in the direction sense: southern Italy; after a verb in the 'American South' sense: Her family is very Southern
entries.comparison: not gradable — but the 'American South' sense grades: very Southern, more Southern; the farthest south is southernmost
entries.form: -ern from south, with the vowel changed
entries.contrast: The vowel changes: south is SOWTH, but Southern is SUH-thurn, and the SOW- vowel is the most common mistake with this word. Capital Southern means the American South, roughly from Texas and Virginia down to Florida: Southern hospitality, Southern cooking, a Southern accent. Plain direction is lowercase: southern Italy, the southern tip of Florida. The person is a Southerner.

examples: We're reading a Victorian novel by Charles Dickens.
They restored a Victorian house with a wraparound porch.
San Francisco is famous for its painted Victorian row houses.
My grandparents had very Victorian ideas about dating.
The school's dress code is more Victorian than anyone expected.

senses.head: Of the time when Queen Victoria ruled Britain, 1837 to 1901, or in the ornate style of its houses and furniture
examples: We're reading a Victorian novel by Charles Dickens.
They restored a Victorian house with a wraparound porch.
San Francisco is famous for its painted Victorian row houses.

senses.head: Strict and old-fashioned about morals, especially about sex
examples: My grandparents had very Victorian ideas about dating.
The school's dress code is more Victorian than anyone expected.

entries.position: both — a Victorian house, Their ideas about dating are very Victorian
entries.comparison: not gradable — but the 'strict about morals' sense grades: very Victorian, more Victorian
entries.contrast: In American English a Victorian (a noun) is usually a house built in that period: They bought a Victorian on Elm Street. The word names a British queen, but Americans use it for their own late 19th-century houses and manners too. The 'prudish' sense is critical, and it sounds a little old-fashioned itself.

examples: She's a trained Shakespearean actor.
A Shakespearean sonnet has fourteen lines.
Students struggle with Shakespearean English at first.
The family feud had become a tragedy of Shakespearean proportions.
The senator's downfall was almost Shakespearean.

senses.head: Of William Shakespeare or his plays and poems
examples: She's a trained Shakespearean actor.
A Shakespearean sonnet has fourteen lines.
Students struggle with Shakespearean English at first.

senses.head: Like the events of Shakespeare's plays, especially tragic on a grand scale
examples: The family feud had become a tragedy of Shakespearean proportions.
The senator's downfall was almost Shakespearean.

entries.position: both — mostly before a noun: a Shakespearean actor; after a verb in the 'grand and tragic' sense: His downfall was almost Shakespearean
entries.contrast: American spelling is Shakespearean; Shakespearian is a British variant. A Shakespearean actor is one who often plays Shakespeare, not a character from the plays. Russian шекспировские страсти is a drama of Shakespearean proportions.
